summary: The actual Gauss singleton is not G_delta. Its bounded USC indicator admits no decreasing continuous presentation and lies outside ENTIRE original G. No psh assignment or prescribed-equation nonexistence follows.
detailedSummary: Every countable family of Gauss neighbourhoods involves only countably many Laurent-polynomial norm constraints. Algebraically independent constants over their countable residue-coefficient field produce another rigid point satisfying every constraint. Thus the Gauss singleton is not G_delta. Its USC indicator would require a cozero complementary sublevel under any decreasing continuous presentation, a contradiction. This excludes all original-G presentations, but does not reject a psh variational candidate or solve the isotropic Dirac equation.
text:
An actual-carrier obstruction to every decreasing continuous presentation, hence the ENTIRE original G.

On the exact surface and original class of OWN n1, let g be the image of the joint unit Gauss point of z1,z2. THEOREM: {g} is not a G_delta subset of the actual ordinary analytic topology of X. The bounded function u_g(g)=1 and u_g(y)=0 for y!=g is consequently upper semicontinuous but admits no pointwise decreasing sequence of ordinary real continuous functions. In particular u_g is outside ENTIRE original G, irrespective of energy bounds. It is not declared psh, finite energy or an equation potential.

Proof. On the torus let V={|r_i|<1/4}. The deck element (m,n) multiplies coordinates by (t^m 3^n,2^m t^n), translating r by (m,n), since |2|=|3|=1 and |t|=exp(-1). Distinct translates of V are disjoint. The quotient topology identifies V homeomorphically with its ordinary open image. This is a topological chart assertion, not coherent descent or nonalgebraization.

Take any countable collection of open neighbourhoods of g and lift them to V. The defining seminorm topology of affine torus analytification is the weakest topology making evaluations |P| for P in K[z1^+/-1,z2^+/-1] continuous. Each neighbourhood therefore contains a basic neighbourhood specified by finitely many Laurent-polynomial norm conditions. Collect their countably many nonzero polynomials P_l. At g their norms M_l are maximum coefficient norms. Divide each polynomial by a coefficient of norm M_l. The resulting coefficients lie in the valuation ring and its reduction is a nonzero Laurent polynomial over the residue field C.

Let F be the field generated over Q by all coefficients of these reductions. It is countable because finite rational expressions in a countable set form a countable set. Complex elements algebraic over a countable field are countable: there are countably many polynomials, each with finitely many roots. Choose alpha in C transcendental over F, then beta in C transcendental over the countable field F(alpha), using uncountability of C. Thus alpha,beta are nonzero and algebraically independent over F. Each collected reduced Laurent polynomial is nonzero at (alpha,beta), after clearing a monomial denominator.

At the rigid point p=(alpha,beta), viewed as constants in K, both coordinates have norm one. Every normalized polynomial evaluation has nonzero residue and therefore norm one. Hence |P_l(p)|=M_l=|P_l(g)| for ALL l. The point p belongs to V and every chosen basic neighbourhood, thus every original neighbourhood. It differs from g because |z1-alpha|(p)=0 but |z1-alpha|(g)=1. Local injectivity preserves this distinction in X. Therefore no countable intersection of open neighbourhoods isolates g.

Since X is Hausdorff, {g} is closed and its indicated singleton indicator is upper semicontinuous. If this indicator admitted a decreasing continuous presentation, OWN n1's proved cozero barrier lemma would make {u_g<1/2}=X minus {g} a cozero set. Its complement would then be the zero set of continuous nonnegative f, equal to the countable intersection of open sets {f<1/n}. This contradicts the preceding result. Thus NO original-C sequence presentation exists. The obstruction tests all ordinary continuous presentations, hence ENTIRE G, rather than a radial, fan or pencil subclass.

The proof uses the actual defining seminorm topology, explicit deck translations, elementary reduction/countability arguments and OWN n1's barrier lemma. No supplied note is a correctness grant. Supplied geometry remains input; genuine nonalgebraization and coherent descent remain uncertified. The complete proof is in recognition-bridge.tex and complete-proof-companion.txt; its definition-only topological application is recorded in source-application-reading-ledger.json.

This demonstrates that upper semicontinuity alone cannot guarantee the actual sequence antecedent. It does not test a constructed psh target for OLD 2delta_x_(1/8), and does not imply nonexistence of that equation or of arbitrary-support finite-energy equations.
